coverage: CATCH-UP RUN: Thursday 10 Sep 2026, ~18:10-18:55 SGT (an evening run, not the usual pre-Asia-open slot) after the prior run 4 Sep 2026 -- a 6-calendar-day / 4-trading-session gap. NY is currently Thu 06:10am (pre-market; the latest COMPLETED US session is Wed 9 Sep). Asia (HK/JP/KR/SG) all closed today. The week reversed much of the 3 Sep dovish-pivot rally: a blowout +162K NFP (vs 55K consensus, 5 Sep) revived a hike-not-cut debate for the Sep 15-16 FOMC as new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish tone squares off against Governor Waller's dovish dissent. The S&P 500 fell three of four sessions since 3 Sep (-1.44% cumulative to 7636.36) as the 10y yield spiked to 4.857% (highest since Nov 2023) on 9 Sep after the Treasury tripled its long-dated debt buyback. The Hormuz/Iran war escalated rather than resolved -- fresh IRGC strikes on vessels including US ships, Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure, Brent topping $100 for the first time in six weeks -- while gold/silver miners fully reversed the 2 Sep Barrick-led governance dip. Xiaomi fell 8.9% on the week on concrete operating weakness (EV delivery shortfall, revenue's first y/y decline in ~3 years) despite its 7 Sep product blitz. US market internals deteriorated sharply (CNN Fear&Greed 36.3/Fear vs 64.7/Greed a month ago). PPI (today) and CPI (tomorrow) are the immediate swing data into the FOMC.
tldr: A blowout +162K NFP (vs 55K consensus) revived a genuine HIKE debate for the Sep 15-16 FOMC as new Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish tone squares off against Governor Waller's dovish dissent -- PPI prints today, CPI tomorrow, both decisive swing data.

The S&P 500 gave back its early-Sep rally over three sessions (-1.44% cumulative) and US market internals deteriorated sharply (CNN Fear&Greed fell to 36.3/Fear from 64.7/Greed a month ago; %S&P500>50-DMA cratered to 36.97%) -- a genuine, not just index-level, weakening.

The Hormuz/Iran war is escalating, not de-escalating -- fresh IRGC strikes on vessels including US ships, Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure, and Brent above $100 for the first time in six weeks; Eurasia Group now expects real de-escalation only by year-end.

Gold/silver miners fully reversed the 2 Sep Barrick-led governance dip, with Barrick rallying back to $49.33 by 9 Sep alongside a broad miners surge on renewed haven demand -- the levered silver/miners sleeve remains the strongest-conviction part of the book.

Xiaomi fell 8.9% on the week specifically -- its 7 Sep product blitz (Xiaomi 18 Fold, Sky Nomad EVs) failed to offset concrete operating weakness (EV deliveries tracking only 44.8% of the FY target, revenue's first y/y decline in ~3 years) -- while Tencent and SMIC fell on shared macro pressure.

Crypto drifted lower (BTC -4.1% to ~$77,944) even as crypto-specific Fear&Greed stayed at 69/Greed (vs equities' 36/Fear) -- a genuine sentiment divergence -- while the Sep 15 CLARITY Act cloture-vote odds deteriorated further to ~10-25%, landing the same day as the FOMC decision.
